evidence.note: Systematic boto3-driven verification per subsystem right after building: smoke tests, multi-tenant/quota/presigned/versioning, policy/CORS/multi-delete/audit, console API, and a dedicated concurrency test (53) for the 30-client requirement.
Grader-condition-specific probes: lifecycle expiry via fast-clock env restart (57,76), bucket notification webhook delivery (78), multipart edge cases including ETag/EntityTooSmall (85,87).

Re-tests after code fixes (pagination 94, start-after 96, anonymous HEAD 98/105) and a dedicated UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD signing test (111) — mirroring specific boto3/SigV4 grader conditions and re-verifying to catch regressions.
Full regression run and audit-log format validation near the end, showing repeated green-check discipline rather than one-shot poking.
Console verified only via its API endpoints; no browser DOM/testid assertions, a gap given the dimension's explicit emphasis on the console data-testid contract.

reasoning: The agent went well past the level-5 anchor: it used real boto3 across the main data plane, added a concurrency test for the 30-client rule, and probed edge cases (multipart ETag, pagination, anonymous HEAD) plus grader-specific conditions like UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, presigned, notification delivery, fast-clock lifecycle, and audit format — with re-runs after fixes and a full regression pass, matching and exceeding the level-8 description. It falls short of 10 because console verification is API-only (no DOM/testid assertions), audit atomicity under concurrency isn't clearly tested, and the checks are ad hoc scripts rather than a formalized reusable harness. That places it solidly at 8.
